summary: Trace one declared P or S geometric ray through flat constant-velocity layers while keeping travel time, interface refraction and phenomenological Q_x attenuation explicit.
objective: Build a bounded ray inspector where I change takeoff angle, layer velocity and Q_x, then see valid segments, travel time and amplitude ledger or a critical-interface rejection.
example_prompts: Trace a 5 Hz P ray across three flat layers and show each refraction, segment time and Q loss.
negative_signals: Not a wavefront solver, whole-Earth model, inversion, earthquake forecast or hazard estimate.
not_for: No reflection amplitude, mode conversion, diffraction, scattering, geometric spreading, anisotropy or spherical Earth.

entities.name: Layer stack
entities.guidance: Blender authors flat slabs and named interfaces; a data table owns thickness, chosen P-or-S velocity and propagating-wave Q_x for each layer.

entities.name: Ray ledger
entities.guidance: Three.js solves one coplanar path and lists angle from interface normal, segment length/time and Q_x attenuation exponent per segment.

state_contract.model: Use N flat horizontal layers with positive thickness hi, phase velocity vi, propagating-wave attenuation factor Qx_i and one frequency f>0; layers are nondispersive within this authored monochromatic model. Angles are measured from the interface normal. Preserve the ray parameter p=sin(theta_i)/vi across transmitted segments. Reject a requested transmission when |p*vi|>1. When |p*vi|=1 within tolerance, label a grazing segment and terminate because it cannot cross the next positive-thickness horizontal layer; do not invent a converted or reflected branch. For a segment of length ell_i, travel time Ti=ell_i/vi. This teaching model declares amplitude multiplier exp(-pi*f*Ti/Qx_i) per segment, so log amplitude accumulates -pi*f*sum(Ti/Qx_i); this is an explicit constant-Q phenomenological law, excluding spreading and interface coefficients.
state_contract.authority: Three.js owns units, ray solve, validity, travel-time and log-amplitude ledger. Blender owns layer slabs, interface planes and source/receiver markers; mesh scale is not velocity.
actions: Choose P or S and one finite flat layer table.
Change takeoff angle and recompute every downstream segment atomically.
Inspect a rejected critical interface without extending the ray.
Change f or Q_x and update amplitude only, leaving path and travel time invariant.

invariants: p is constant on every accepted transmitted segment within tolerance.
All segment times are positive and total time is their sum.
Changing f or Q_x cannot change the geometric path in this nondispersive authored model.
An asin argument above one rejects without a partial downstream path; equality within tolerance produces a labeled grazing termination, not a positive-thickness crossing.
motion_guidance: Play, pause and step advance the declared model clock only; reset restores parameters, state, solver budget, selections, errors and presentation transforms.
Use static before/after states and numeric tables for reduced motion; animation interpolates committed state and never supplies physical evidence.
creative_affordances: Blender may shape distinctive apparatus, cutaways and materials; Three.js binds named parts to authoritative state and keeps units and error states readable.
Camera, color, trails and deformation gain are presentation controls and cannot change the numerical model.
known_limits: Flat, piecewise homogeneous, nondispersive scalar ray only; the Q_x amplitude law is a declared lesson model, not a calibrated site prediction.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no Blender export, numerical simulation, contact solve, browser or renderer was run.

claims.statement: For optical refraction, Snell’s law uses angles from the interface normal and n1*sin(theta1)=n2*sin(theta2); because refractive index is inversely related to wave speed, the speed form preserves sin(theta)/v. This recipe explicitly adopts that form as its scalar flat-layer ray law.
claims.scope: Source-backed optical refraction relation used as a declared geometric-wave model; no seismic interface amplitude, reflection or P/S mode conversion is claimed.

source_refs.locator: Section 1.3, law of refraction and speed-change explanation around equation 1.4

claims.statement: P and S body waves have material-dependent velocities, with P particle motion parallel and S motion transverse in a homogeneous elastic medium.
claims.scope: Choice of one P or S velocity per layer; no claim that optical refractive index equals seismic material data.

source_refs.locator: Body-wave overview and P/S velocity relations

claims.statement: For a propagating monochromatic wave, the cited paper defines spatial attenuation factor Q_x so amplitude diminishes with distance x as exp(-pi*x/(c*T*Q_x)), distinct from the standing-wave time-decay factor Q_T. With T=1/f and segment travel time x/c, this equals exp(-pi*f*time/Q_x).
claims.scope: Piecewise application to this recipe’s nondispersive constant-velocity segments; Q_x values are declared inputs, and no inference, dispersion, interface loss, spreading or calibration is claimed.

source_refs.locator: Abstract: definitions of Q_T and Q_x and exponential amplitude laws for standing and propagating monochromatic waves

object_craft.structure: Use dimensioned slabs, interface-normal arrows and one continuous segmented tube; stop the tube visibly at an invalid interface.
object_craft.material: Assign layers readable patterns and label path attenuation numerically; opacity does not stand for Q.

physical_contract.scope: Flat-layer geometric transmission path plus declared constant-Q amplitude bookkeeping.
physical_contract.timestep: No integration; recompute path and ledger from immutable inputs.
state: ray kind, frequency and takeoff angle
